sentences: Credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, accounting for about 27% of the model's importance, and risk rises steadily as the share of the credit limit in use grows.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk jumps once an applicant has at least one delinquency.

The effect of credit utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies, so high utilization matters much more for applicants with several delinquencies, while utilization shows no practical interaction with income or credit history length.
Income has a moderate effect, and default risk decreases as income rises.
The length of credit history also has a moderate effect, with risk decreasing as history gets longer, and it matters more than the debt-to-income ratio.
The debt-to-income ratio is the fifth most important feature, with a weak to moderate effect in which risk increases with the ratio.
Recent credit inquiries have at most a weak effect, with risk increasing slightly as their number grows.
Age and months at the current address hardly matter, and the number of dependents has at most a weak effect.
